requirements.text: Change the image into pencil drawing
requirements.source_phrase: Change the image into pencil drawing

outcomes.description: Transform the image into a pencil drawing.
outcomes.target: The image is rendered as a pencil drawing, with its visual content represented in a pencil-drawn style.
outcomes.reference: The supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show the original scene rendered overall as a pencil drawing, rather than merely receiving muted color, grain, or softened photographic shading?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when comparison with the source shows the scene's visual content rendered overall in a pencil-drawn style; muted or desaturated color, grain, and softened edges alone do not suffice. Fail when there is sufficient evidence that the scene remains substantially photographic without an overall pencil-drawing rendering. Unknown if the comparison or style cannot be assessed reliably. Do not require monochrome or a particular pencil technique.
nodes.binding: Compare the source and edited images across the scene, including the food and surrounding setting. Judge the overall rendering, not isolated texture cues; cite concrete visual evidence and distinguish drawing-like rendering from retained photographic structure, shading, or reflections.

nodes.question: Is there image-grounded evidence of any relevant progress toward rendering the content as a pencil drawing, even if the overall transformation is incomplete?
nodes.criteria: Pass if visible changes move the image toward a pencil-drawn rendering, including partial stylization; fail if sufficient evidence shows no requested transformation has progressed; unknown if evidence is insufficient. Muted color, grain, or softened edges may support progress but do not establish completion. Unrelated edits do not count.
nodes.binding: Assess only visible changes in the supplied image relative to the source that move its visual content toward a pencil-drawn style. Do not decide completion or infer progress from unrelated changes.

nodes.question: Does the image visibly appear as a completed pencil drawing?
nodes.criteria: Compose both supports under R1 without treating either support as completion credit by itself. Complete (yes) only when s1 passes. Partial only when s1 does not pass, s2 passes, and the evidence is sufficient to establish some requested progress without complete fulfillment. Absent (no) only when s1 fails and s2 fails, with sufficient evidence that no requested change has progressed. Unknown when required evidence is unresolved, including when s1 is unknown and completion cannot be established, or when s2 is unknown and absence or partial progress cannot be established. Unrelated edits never count as progress.
nodes.binding: Target: The image is rendered as a pencil drawing, with its visual content represented in a pencil-drawn style.. Reference: The supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
